outputs.L1: A power conditioning system comprising: a fuel cell configured to be connected to a load; a fuel cell converter connected between the fuel cell and the load, the fuel cell converter being configured to convert an output voltage of the fuel cell at a predetermined required voltage ratio; a battery connected in parallel with the fuel cell with respect to the load, the battery serving as a power supply source different from the fuel cell; a battery converter connected between the battery and the load, the battery converter being configured to convert an output voltage of the battery at a predetermined required voltage ratio; a voltage adjusting unit configured to adjust an output voltage of the battery converter to a predetermined voltage, thereby generating a DC link voltage for synchronizing an output voltage of the fuel cell converter with the output voltage of the battery converter; and a ripple suppressing unit configured to cause the battery converter to suppress a ripple component of the DC link voltage when the DC link voltage is higher than the output voltage of the battery.
outputs.L2: A power conditioning apparatus comprises a fuel cell configured for connection to a load and a fuel cell converter arranged between the fuel cell and the load, the fuel cell converter being configured to transform the fuel cell’s output voltage according to a preset required voltage ratio. The apparatus further includes a battery coupled in parallel with the fuel cell relative to the load, the battery functioning as an electrical supply source separate from the fuel cell, and a battery converter disposed between the battery and the load, the battery converter being configured to convert the battery’s output voltage according to a preset required voltage ratio. The apparatus also includes a voltage regulation unit that sets the output voltage of the battery converter to a predetermined level so as to form a DC link voltage for matching the output voltage of the fuel cell converter with the output voltage of the battery converter. In addition, a ripple reduction unit is provided to control the battery converter to reduce a ripple component contained in the DC link voltage when the DC link voltage exceeds the output voltage of the battery.
outputs.L3:
The power conditioning system includes a fuel cell that is electrically connected to a load through a fuel cell converter. The fuel cell functions as a primary power supply source, while the fuel cell converter adjusts the electrical output of the fuel cell before the power is delivered to the load.

The fuel cell converter is configured to convert the output voltage of the fuel cell according to a predetermined required voltage ratio. By performing this voltage conversion, the fuel cell converter ensures that the voltage supplied from the fuel cell is appropriately matched to the operating requirements of the load or to the voltage level required within the power conditioning system.

In addition to the fuel cell, a battery is connected in parallel with the fuel cell. The battery serves as an additional power supply source and can support the fuel cell when extra power is required, during transient load changes, or when stabilization of the system voltage is needed. This parallel arrangement allows the system to draw power from either the fuel cell, the battery, or both, depending on operating conditions.

The battery is connected through a battery converter, which converts the output voltage of the battery. The battery converter contributes to the generation of a DC link voltage used for synchronization within the system. By regulating the battery output voltage, the battery converter helps maintain a suitable DC voltage level for coordinated operation between the fuel cell, the battery, and the load.

The system further includes a ripple suppressing unit. This ripple suppressing unit controls the battery converter so that the battery converter suppresses ripple components in the DC link voltage when the DC link voltage is higher than the battery output voltage. As a result, fluctuations in the DC link voltage can be reduced, improving voltage stability and enhancing the overall reliability and performance of the power conditioning system.
outputs.L4:
A power conditioning system may be configured to manage and combine power supplied from a fuel cell and a battery connected in parallel. The system includes a fuel cell converter associated with the fuel cell, a battery converter associated with the battery, and a voltage adjusting unit that controls a DC link voltage shared between the converters. By adjusting the DC link voltage to an appropriate level, the voltage adjusting unit enables the output of the fuel cell converter and the output of the battery converter to be synchronized and supplied together to a common load.

In operation, the fuel cell can provide a primary source of electrical power, while the battery can supplement the fuel cell when additional power is required or absorb excess energy when conditions permit. The dedicated converters regulate the respective output voltages and currents of the fuel cell and the battery so that both sources can operate efficiently and safely despite differences in their electrical characteristics.

The voltage adjusting unit plays an important coordinating role by setting the DC link voltage at a level suitable for stable power transfer. When the DC link voltage is higher than the output voltage of the battery, the battery converter operates to reduce or suppress ripple components appearing in the DC link voltage. This ripple suppression helps prevent fluctuations from being transmitted to the load and supports a more stable and reliable power supply.

As a result, the power conditioning system can improve the quality of power delivered to the load while maintaining coordinated operation between the fuel cell and the battery. The arrangement allows the fuel cell to operate smoothly, enables the battery to respond to transient load changes, and reduces voltage instability in the DC link, thereby enhancing the overall performance and reliability of the power delivery system.
outputs.L5:
**A Power Conditioning System**

A power conditioning system is an important device used to improve the quality and reliability of electrical power. It helps ensure that electronic equipment receives a stable, clean, and safe supply of electricity. In many homes, offices, factories, and data centers, power fluctuations can damage sensitive devices or reduce their performance. Power conditioning helps prevent these problems.

Power conditioning can include several functions, such as voltage regulation, surge protection, noise filtering, and power factor correction. Voltage regulation keeps the voltage at a safe and consistent level, even when the incoming power supply changes. Surge protection guards equipment against sudden increases in voltage, which can happen during lightning strikes or electrical faults. Noise filtering removes electrical interference that may affect computers, communication systems, or medical equipment.

A power conditioning system is especially useful for sensitive devices such as servers, laboratory instruments, industrial machines, and audio-visual equipment. In industrial environments, unstable power can cause machines to stop unexpectedly, resulting in production delays and financial losses. In data centers, poor power quality can lead to system failures or data loss.

There are different types of power conditioning devices, including voltage regulators, uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), line conditioners, and isolation transformers. Some systems are simple and designed for small appliances, while others are complex and built for large industrial or commercial use.

In conclusion, power conditioning plays a vital role in protecting electrical equipment and improving power quality. By providing stable and clean electricity, it helps extend the life of devices, reduce downtime, and support efficient operation in many different settings.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal patent abstract describing a hybrid fuel-cell/battery power conditioning apparatus where the battery converter adjusts DC link voltage and suppresses ripple when the link voltage exceeds the battery output voltage.
counterfactuals.output: A hybrid fuel-cell/battery power conditioning apparatus is provided for supplying regulated electrical power to a load through a DC link. The apparatus includes a fuel-cell power source coupled to the DC link by a fuel-cell converter, a battery coupled to the DC link by a bidirectional battery converter, and a controller configured to coordinate operation of the converters. The battery converter is operated to adjust the DC link voltage and to attenuate voltage or current ripple on the DC link when the DC link voltage is greater than an output voltage of the battery. In this operating condition, the battery converter selectively transfers energy between the DC link and the battery while providing active ripple suppression, thereby reducing dynamic loading of the fuel cell and improving stability of the DC link. The controller may regulate duty cycles, switching states, or current references of the battery converter in response to sensed DC link voltage, battery voltage, and ripple components. The apparatus thereby enables improved transient response, reduced fuel-cell stress, and enhanced power quality in hybrid electric power systems.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.output: A system for stabilizing a DC link voltage supplied to a load, comprising: a fuel cell converter configured to convert electrical power generated by a fuel cell into a regulated DC output supplied to a DC link; a battery converter configured to exchange electrical power between a battery and the DC link; a voltage adjusting unit operatively coupled to at least one of the fuel cell converter and the battery converter and configured to adjust an output voltage or duty ratio thereof based on a deviation between a detected DC link voltage and a target DC link voltage; and a ripple suppressing unit configured to detect or estimate voltage ripple or current ripple associated with the DC link and to generate a compensation signal applied to the fuel cell converter, the battery converter, or the voltage adjusting unit, wherein the fuel cell converter, the battery converter, the voltage adjusting unit, and the ripple suppressing unit cooperatively regulate power flow from the fuel cell and the battery to the load so as to maintain the DC link voltage substantially at the target DC link voltage while suppressing ripple components in the DC link voltage.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for a fuel cell power supply system with a secondary battery and DC/DC converters, emphasizing required voltage ratios, synchronization of converter outputs, and suppression of DC link ripple components.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention is provided for a fuel-cell power supply system capable of stably supplying electric power to a load, such as a vehicle drive inverter, while reducing voltage fluctuation on a DC link.

The system includes:

- a fuel cell stack serving as a main DC power source;
- a secondary battery, such as a lithium-ion battery, serving as an auxiliary power source and energy buffer;
- a first DC/DC converter connected between the fuel cell and a DC link;
- a second DC/DC converter connected between the secondary battery and the DC link; and
- a controller configured to control the output voltages, switching phases, and power sharing of the converters.

The DC link supplies power to a load, for example an inverter driving an electric motor.

In one embodiment, the first DC/DC converter boosts the voltage of the fuel cell to the DC link voltage, and the second DC/DC converter performs bidirectional conversion between the battery and the DC link. The voltage conversion ratios of the converters are selected so that the required boost ratio of the fuel-cell-side converter and the required charge/discharge ratio of the battery-side converter remain within efficient operating ranges. In particular, the system is configured such that the DC link voltage is higher than the fuel cell output voltage and also higher than the rated battery voltage, while the ratio between the DC link voltage and each source voltage is limited to a predetermined range. This avoids excessive duty ratios, reduces switching loss, and improves controllability.

A control unit synchronizes the switching operation or output-current ripple phases of the first and second DC/DC converters. The converters are operated at the same switching frequency or at frequencies having an integer relationship. Their switching phases are controlled so that ripple components generated by the converters at the DC link are mutually offset. For example, the output ripple current of the fuel-cell-side converter and the output ripple current of the battery-side converter may be phase-shifted by approximately 180 degrees, or by another phase angle selected according to the number of phases and converter topology, so that their AC ripple components cancel each other on the DC link.

The controller may detect or estimate DC link ripple voltage or ripple current and adjust the phase relationship between the converters in response. When the operating point of the fuel cell, the battery, or the load changes, the controller changes the duty ratio and/or phase of the converters while maintaining synchronization. As a result, the DC component required by the load is supplied reliably, while high-frequency ripple components flowing into the DC link capacitor are reduced.

By suppressing ripple components on the DC link, the invention reduces stress on smoothing capacitors, decreases electromagnetic noise, improves inverter input stability, and allows reduction in size and cost of the DC link capacitor. The secondary battery also absorbs transient load variations and regenerative energy, thereby allowing the fuel cell to operate in a more stable and efficient region.

Thus, the invention provides a fuel cell power supply apparatus in which required voltage conversion ratios are properly set, converter outputs are synchronized, and DC link ripple components are actively suppressed through coordinated control of multiple DC/DC converters.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following concept into patent-claim language: fuel cell and battery power sources feed a common load through separate converters; the battery converter sets a DC link voltage and suppresses ripple when the DC link is above battery voltage.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A power supply system comprising:**

   a fuel cell power source;

   a battery power source;

   a DC link configured to supply electrical power to a common load;

   a first power converter coupled between the fuel cell power source and the DC link and configured to transfer power from the fuel cell power source to the DC link; and

   a second power converter coupled between the battery power source and the DC link,

   wherein the second power converter is configured to regulate a voltage of the DC link to a predetermined DC link voltage, and

   wherein, when the predetermined DC link voltage is greater than a voltage of the battery power source, the second power converter is further configured to suppress voltage ripple on the DC link.

2. **The power supply system of claim 1**, wherein the second power converter comprises a bidirectional DC-DC converter configured to selectively deliver power from the battery power source to the DC link and absorb power from the DC link into the battery power source.

3. **The power supply system of claim 1**, wherein the first power converter is controlled to provide fuel-cell power to the common load while the second power converter maintains the DC link voltage.

4. **The power supply system of claim 1**, wherein the second power converter is configured to suppress the voltage ripple by controlling current exchanged between the battery power source and the DC link.

5. **The power supply system of claim 1**, wherein the common load comprises an inverter, motor drive, or other DC-link-connected electrical load.
